name: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
duration_note: The final year is largely given over to practical training under ICAR's Student READY component (village attachment, experiential learning, industry or institutional attachment). The Sixth Deans Committee framework also describes NEP-style exit points with internships after the early years; how and whether a university offers them varies.

hero.summary: A four-year professional degree that covers crop production, soil, plant protection, genetics, farm economics and extension. Students spend a lot of time on college farms and in laboratories, and the final year moves into village attachment and hands-on enterprise training under ICAR's Student READY model.

overview.heading: What the B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture degree covers
paragraphs: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture is the core professional degree of India's agricultural university system. Most programmes follow the course structure recommended by ICAR's Deans Committees. The Sixth Deans Committee report, published in volumes on ICAR's e-book portal, restructured the undergraduate curricula to fit the National Education Policy 2020. That means more skill-enhancement courses, credit transfer and defined exit points.

The programme combines plant, animal and social sciences. Students study agronomy, soil science, plant breeding, entomology, plant pathology, horticulture, agricultural economics and extension education. Lectures run alongside farm work and laboratory practicals. Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), for example, describes its version as four years of coursework with farm and laboratory exposure, industry internships and experiential learning courses run on an earn-while-you-learn basis.

The degree is offered by state agricultural universities, central agricultural universities, ICAR deemed universities, and general and private universities with agriculture faculties. Seats, admission rules, fees and course titles depend on the institution. Applicants should check each university's current prospectus and ICAR accreditation status before applying.

who_should_apply: Students who studied biology, agriculture or mathematics in Class 12 alongside physics and chemistry and want to apply science to food production
Applicants who are comfortable with outdoor field work, seasonal farm schedules and laboratory practicals
Students interested in rural development, farmer advisory work or extension communication
Those planning a career in agri-input, seed or food businesses, or aiming for agricultural research through postgraduate study
Aspiring agri-entrepreneurs who want structured exposure to farm enterprises before starting their own

curriculum.heading: How the four years are organised
curriculum.intro: The curriculum follows the ICAR Deans Committee model, but each university adapts course titles, credit loads and the semester in which a course is taught. The outline below shows typical subject areas only. Check your university's own course catalogue for exact names and credits.

structure.focus: Basic sciences and introductory agricultural disciplines alongside common and skill-enhancement courses.
courses: Introductory crop physiology and plant biochemistry
Fundamentals of entomology and plant pathology
Agricultural economics and rural sociology basics

structure.focus: Applied courses on crops, soils, pests, diseases, breeding, farm machinery and markets.
courses: Principles of plant breeding and seed technology
Agricultural marketing, finance and farm management

structure.focus: Mostly practical work in villages, institutional farms, industry and enterprise modules.

practical_learning.name: Rural Agricultural Work Experience (RAWE)
practical_learning.description: Students are attached to villages and partner agencies to study farming systems, diagnose field problems and take part in extension activities with farmers.

practical_learning.name: Experiential Learning Programme (ELP)
practical_learning.description: Small teams run a production or service unit, such as seed production, biofertiliser or biocontrol inputs, protected cultivation or value addition, from planning through to sale.

practical_learning.name: Industry / institutional attachment
practical_learning.description: Short placements with agri-input, seed, processing or research organisations to see how work is done outside the campus.

practical_learning.name: Farm and laboratory practicals
practical_learning.description: Regular field practicals on instructional farms and laboratory classes run alongside the theory courses from the first year.

points: Class 12 (10+2) or equivalent from a recognised board is the base requirement for entry to the four-year degree.
For ICAR-quota seats through CUET-UG (2025 cycle), candidates needed at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture in Class 12, and had to take the same subjects in CUET.

The ICAR-quota minimum aggregate in Class 12 was 50% for General, OBC-NCL, EWS and UPS candidates, and 40% for SC, ST, PwBD and third-gender candidates, with no rounding off (2025 cycle; confirm in the current bulletin).
ICAR-quota candidates had to be at least 16 years old on the cut-off date stated in the bulletin (31 August of the admission year in the 2025 cycle).

State-quota seats follow state rules. Subject combinations, domicile requirements, reservation and minimum marks vary by state and university. Some states also run separate entry routes for agriculture diploma holders.

routes.name: CUET-UG (ICAR quota seats)
routes.description: ICAR uses CUET-UG scores, with the test run by NTA, to fill its all-India quota through online counselling. In the 2025 cycle this covered 20% of seats in participating state agricultural universities and all seats in ICAR deemed universities and central agricultural universities.

routes.name: State agricultural entrance / counselling
routes.description: Most remaining seats go through state processes. Depending on the state, this means a state entrance test, a common engineering-and-agriculture test, or merit in Class 12 marks. For example, ANGRAU (Andhra Pradesh) published 2026 counselling for B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture using AP EAPCET ranks and, separately, AP AGRICET ranks.

routes.name: University entrance or merit
routes.description: Private and deemed universities with agriculture faculties usually admit through their own entrance test or qualifying-exam merit. Check whether the programme is ICAR-accredited before applying.

exams.name: CUET-UG
exams.note: Used for ICAR all-India quota counselling. Pick domain subjects that match your Class 12 subjects.

exams.name: State-level agriculture or common entrance tests
exams.note: Names and patterns differ by state, for example AP EAPCET and AP AGRICET in Andhra Pradesh.

steps.title: Shortlist routes
steps.text: Decide whether you are applying for ICAR quota seats, your home-state seats, private universities, or more than one.

steps.title: Match CUET subjects to Class 12
steps.text: If you are taking CUET-UG, choose domain subjects that match the core subjects on your Class 12 marksheet.

steps.title: Register for counselling
steps.text: After results, register separately for ICAR counselling and any state counselling, fill in your choices, and track the round schedules.

steps.title: Verify documents and report
steps.text: Complete document verification, pay the seat acceptance or admission fee within the deadline, and report to the allotted college.

documents: Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets and certificates are usually requested
Category, EWS or PwBD certificates where a reservation is claimed
Domicile or nativity proof for state-quota seats

fees.summary: Fees differ widely. State agricultural universities generally charge government-regulated fees, which still differ between states and between government and self-financing seats. Private and deemed universities set their own fees, and these are often much higher. Hostel, mess, RAWE travel and examination charges may be billed separately. Use the current official fee notice of each institution.

careers.heading: Where agriculture graduates work
careers.intro: Graduates work in farm advisory, input supply, banking, research support and food businesses, and some start their own ventures. Government jobs are filled through competitive recruitment, and postgraduate study opens research and teaching roles. Outcomes depend on the individual, the institution and recruitment cycles.

roles.title: Agriculture officer / extension officer
roles.description: Works with state agriculture departments to deliver schemes, advisories and demonstrations to farmers.

roles.title: Agricultural field officer (banking)
roles.description: Assesses and monitors farm and rural loans for banks.

roles.title: Agri-input sales and technical executive
roles.description: Supports dealers and farmers on seeds, fertilisers and crop-protection products.

roles.title: Seed production and quality staff
roles.description: Organises seed multiplication, field inspection and quality testing for seed companies or agencies.

roles.title: Agri-clinic or agri-business entrepreneur
roles.description: Runs an advisory, input, nursery or value-addition enterprise.

sectors: Research institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras
public_sector_routes: IBPS Specialist Officer – Agricultural Field Officer
State public service commission agriculture officer examinations
ICAR AIEEA (PG) for postgraduate admission and fellowships
ASRB NET after a relevant master's degree (for teaching eligibility)
higher_study: M.Sc. (Agriculture) in agronomy, soil science, entomology, plant pathology, genetics and plant breeding, agricultural economics, extension and other disciplines
MBA / PG diploma in agribusiness management
M.Sc. in biotechnology, environmental science or remote sensing

skills: Farm records, costs and market analysis

faqs.question: Can I apply with PCM instead of PCB?
faqs.answer: Under the ICAR-quota CUET route in the 2025 cycle, any three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture could qualify, so PCM was accepted, provided you took the same subjects in CUET. State and private universities may set different subject rules, so check each prospectus.

faqs.question: Is CUET compulsory for B.Sc. Agriculture?
faqs.answer: Only for ICAR all-India quota seats and for institutions that fill seats through CUET. Most state-quota seats are filled through state entrance tests or state merit counselling, and private universities run their own processes.

faqs.question: What is RAWE?
faqs.answer: Rural Agricultural Work Experience is the village-attachment part of the final-year Student READY programme. Students work with farm families and local agencies to understand field conditions and support extension activities.

faqs.question: Is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture the same as a three-year B.Sc. in agriculture?
faqs.answer: No. The ICAR-model degree is a four-year professional programme. Some public-sector notifications, such as banking agricultural field officer posts, ask for a four-year degree, so check the duration and accreditation of any programme you are considering.

faqs.question: What can I study after B.Sc. Agriculture?
faqs.answer: Common options are an M.Sc. (Agriculture) in a specialised discipline, admission to which ICAR's national PG entrance and university tests support, or an MBA or PG diploma in agribusiness. A Ph.D. can follow later.

faqs.question: Do all universities follow the same syllabus?
faqs.answer: Most agricultural universities base their syllabus on the ICAR Deans Committee recommendations, but they adapt course titles, credits and timing. Your university's academic regulations are the final reference.
